churches.name: Cornerstone Chapel, an Apostolic Church

score_notes.christology: Oneness Apostolic theology rejects the Trinity — teaches Jesus-Only modalism (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not distinct persons but modes of one God = Jesus). This is a historic heresy (condemned at Nicaea/Constantinople).
score_notes.soteriology: Apostolic churches typically teach baptismal regeneration and speaking in tongues as necessary for salvation — 'Acts 2:38 salvation plan' that adds works to justification by faith alone.
score_notes.gender: Male lead pastor (Robert Eaby Jr.); Oneness Pentecostal tradition historically allows women in various ministry roles; no explicit patriarchal household or male-elder-only framework confirmed.
score_notes.denominational: Apostolic/Oneness tradition stands outside Nicene orthodoxy; no accountability to historic trinitarian Christianity.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.
churches.gender_detail: Male lead pastor; Apostolic tradition varies — women's ministry role unclear in Oneness Pentecostalism

churches.assessment: Hope Presbyterian is one of the strongest finds on this list. Pastor Jonathan Dennis holds an MDiv from Reformed Theological Seminary — one of the top conservative Reformed seminaries in the world — and has been in EPC ministry since 2010. The EPC is a conservative evangelical Presbyterian denomination that affirms inerrancy, salvation by faith alone, and Nicene orthodoxy. It sits to the right of mainline Presbyterians (PCUSA) but slightly more latitude than the PCA on women's ordination (letting local congregations set policy). With an RTS-trained lead pastor, the preaching quality and doctrinal grounding should be excellent. The church is mission-focused (Great Commission language throughout) and serves the broader FXBG/Spotsylvania/Stafford/King George area. A serious candidate for Moop's home church search.
churches.gender_detail: EPC allows congregational latitude on women's ordination; complementarian likely but unconfirmed at local level

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg UMC sits squarely in the post-split United Methodist Church — the branch that retained 'United Methodist' branding after the traditional/conservative wing departed to form the Global Methodist Church. The 2024 UMC General Conference removed all language restricting LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage. With a female senior pastor, multiple associate pastors, and UMC denominational accountability to a now-affirming hierarchy, this church does not align with Moop's theological convictions. The congregation may have sincere Christ-loving people in the pews, but the institutional framework is compromised.
churches.gender_detail: Female senior pastor; UMC formally affirms women at all levels and LGBTQ+ clergy/marriage — actively egalitarian

churches.name: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg

score_notes.gender: Calvary Chapel movement holds male pastoral leadership as standard. Mark Ramirez leads as senior pastor; male-only elder/pastor structure is normative in CC churches. Complementarian (halfway house — not fully patriarchal) conviction built into CC DNA.

score_notes.denominational: Calvary Chapel Association is a loose affiliation rather than a formal denomination; provides some accountability but less structured than SBC or PCA.

churches.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The Calvary Chapel movement is known above all for verse-by-verse expository Bible teaching — it's baked into the DNA (Chuck Smith legacy). The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only pastoral leadership; Calvary Chapel maintains complementarian DNA with male elders and pastors

The rector lists she/her pronouns on the church website, men serve with he/him pronouns listed — pronoun-aware staff culture is a visible marker of TEC's progressive institutional identity. Founded in 1877, Trinity has a rich liturgical history and likely has sincere Christians in the congregation, but the denominational framework and leadership culture are incompatible with Moop's convictions. The 'inclusive community of seekers' branding further flags a therapeutic/inclusive ecclesiology rather than a word-and-sacrament Great Commission model. Not recommended.

churches.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

churches.assessment: Selah is a young, Spirit-filled church led by genuinely gospel-loving people. Luke Taylor is a sincere pastor with solid theology on the essentials — Christ is the only way, the Bible is authoritative, gender is binary. But structural concerns are real: no elder accountability, women functioning in pastoral roles, and a spiritual formation emphasis that can trend contemplative rather than expository. If you're a man who needs clear authority structures and complementarian conviction, visit with your eyes open. If you're a new believer or seeking family, you'll find genuine love here. Just ask the hard questions early.

Worth a visit; go in knowing you're in moderate Baptist territory, not SBC.

The mission language is straightforwardly Christ-centered — 'on mission together, striving to continue the work of Christ' with commitments to 'the praise of God and the proclamation of the word of God' and 'the preservation, instruction, and spreading of the Gospel.' That's a healthy public-facing posture. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream, separate from SBC, and the denominational structure allows women in pastoral roles and leans progressive on several fronts. Pastor David Haun's theological convictions are unknown. Before visiting, Moop should confirm the church's stance on Scripture inerrancy, women in ministry, and elder accountability. The Princess Anne address is prime downtown Fredericksburg — a historic congregation worth investigating.

churches.name: Fredericksburg Church of Christ
churches.pastor: Unknown (Churches of Christ tradition does not use 'pastor' title formally — led by elders)
churches.services: Sunday Bible Study 9:00 AM, Sunday Worship 10:00 AM, Wednesday Bible Study 7:00 PM

score_notes.christology: Churches of Christ affirm Christ as the only Savior; Trinitarian orthodoxy affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: Churches of Christ hold a high view of Scripture as the sole rule of faith and practice — this is central to Restoration Movement identity. Their public statement: 'We plead for religious unity among all believers based on the Bible.'
score_notes.gender: Traditional Churches of Christ consistently hold male-only eldership with women not serving in teaching authority over men. This congregation follows the traditional CoC pattern. Green on gender specifically — soteriology is the concern, not gender roles.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led structure is standard in Churches of Christ — a plurality of male elders is the norm, which is more accountable and biblical than single-pastor models.
score_notes.soteriology: Red flag: Churches of Christ historically teach baptismal regeneration — that water baptism (immersion) is necessary for salvation, not just a response to salvation. The classic formula is 'believe + repent + be baptized = receive Holy Spirit + forgiveness.' This adds a work to justification, which is incompatible with faith-alone soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/progressive cultural language found; mission statement is straightforwardly Bible-centered.
score_notes.preaching: Churches of Christ are known for verse-by-verse Bible teaching; expository DNA is strong.
score_notes.denominational: Self-described as non-denominational but part of the Churches of Christ tradition — a distinct stream with its own theological DNA (restoration, baptism, a cappella worship in most congregations).

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only eldership and leadership (Churches of Christ tradition); no women in teaching authority over men

score_notes.christology: Catholic Church affirms Christ as the only Savior; Trinitarian orthodoxy at the highest level — this is Nicene Christianity.
score_notes.scripture: Catholic theology holds Scripture and Sacred Tradition as co-equal sources of revelation — not sola scriptura. The Magisterium (teaching authority of the Church) interprets Scripture authoritatively. This is the classic Protestant/Catholic divide.
score_notes.gender: Roman Catholic Church maintains male-only ordained priesthood — women cannot be priests. However, Catholic teaching does not frame this in terms of biblical patriarchy or husbandly headship in the household; sacramental/apostolic succession theology differs from evangelical complementarian framework. Yellow by framework.
score_notes.leadership: Full hierarchical accountability: parish → diocese → Rome. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane (area dean), signaling senior status. Excellent accountability structure.
score_notes.soteriology: Catholic soteriology includes faith but also sacraments, merit, purgatory, and indulgences — not sola fide. Salvation involves cooperation with grace through the sacramental life of the Church. This is the core Reformation divide.
score_notes.cultural: Diocese of Arlington is one of the most theologically conservative dioceses in the U.S. — less progressive than many other dioceses. No explicit DEI language found on parish website.
score_notes.preaching: Catholic homilies are typically brief (8-12 min), tied to the Sunday Lectionary cycle rather than expository book-by-book preaching.
score_notes.mission: Great Commission is affirmed in Catholic theology; St. Mary is described as 'an active, thriving parish with numerous clubs, organizations, and activities.'
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Knights of Columbus or other men's organizations are standard in active Catholic parishes like St. Mary's.
score_notes.denominational: Excellent accountability: Diocese of Arlington is conservative and supervised; full apostolic succession and diocesan governance.

churches.assessment: Saint Mary's is a large, active Catholic parish in Fredericksburg under the conservative Diocese of Arlington. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane — essentially the area dean — indicating a significant, well-resourced congregation. Trinitarian orthodoxy is rock-solid; male-only priesthood is firmly complementarian; accountability structure is hierarchical and thorough. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the theological divergence is real: Catholic soteriology adds sacraments, merit, and ecclesial mediation to faith; Scripture sits alongside Tradition rather than above it. These are not minor differences — they were the substance of the Reformation. That said, for a man interested in robust liturgy, deep historical tradition, strong pro-life stance, and conservative moral theology, the Diocese of Arlington Catholic experience is among the best available. Not the right fit for a faith-alone evangelical, but should be evaluated on its own terms.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only priesthood (Catholic doctrine) but no explicit biblical patriarchal household framework

churches.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (Old Site) is one of Fredericksburg's most historically significant congregations — founded in 1854 from a congregation dating to the early 1800s, serving the African American community through slavery, the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Civil Rights era. Notable members include John Washington (whose escape from slavery inspired a Trail to Freedom) and Rev. Lawrence A. Davies (pastor and mayor of Fredericksburg). The church's commitment to community (free Wednesday breakfast with Micah Ecumenical Ministries, active youth ministry) reflects genuine love. The honest theological concern is the public framing: 'no barriers to God's grace, no walls of exclusion' and 'inclusive embrace' language combined with minimal gospel-clarity and strong social-service identity suggests the congregation may have drifted toward social gospel territory where the transforming work of Christ is framed primarily in terms of social healing rather than personal salvation and sanctification. This is a pattern in mainline-influenced progressive Baptist churches. Moop should visit and listen to the sermons directly before drawing conclusions.

churches.assessment: Bridge Church Fredericksburg has one of the cleanest statements of faith among the churches surveyed: Trinitarian, Bible as final authority, salvation by grace through faith, baptism as response (not requirement), Great Commission-focused. The church was launched in 2019 by Max Lucado and the Oak Hills Church (San Antonio) team — Jimmy Pruitt was the former campus pastor who was invited by Max to take it independent. That's a vote of confidence from one of the most respected evangelical communicators of our generation. The two-service Sunday model with sermon notes and discipleship resources indicates a substantive ministry rather than a casual social gathering. Main watch items: no explicit complementarian statement, no formal denominational accountability, no confirmed men's ministry. churches.assessment: Common Ground Church has a compelling origin story: 21 years as a mobile congregation finally receiving a permanent home — the historic First Christian Church building on Washington Ave, gifted free of charge by a 100-year-old congregation choosing to bless its successor. That kind of kingdom generosity, and CG's decision to then give their former meeting house (The Old Silk Mill space) to a Filipino congregation, shows genuine missional health. Lead Pastor Gregg Jennings trained at Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (among the most rigorous conservative evangelical seminaries), studied both Theology and Global Missions, and has pastored CG since 2009. The church has elders, active ministries including a men's night, kids, and youth programs. Main yellow flags: Melissa Southall holds a staff pastoral title and was ordained in 2021 (female ordained pastor in a worship/outreach role); the inclusive table language may reflect a broad-welcome posture or a softer ecclesiology — worth hearing a sermon and asking Gregg directly about his complementarian convictions and Scripture inerrancy. The REC/ACNA dual affiliation means accountability in both the richest Reformed Anglican tradition and the broader ACNA network. One of the strongest options for any man who loves liturgy, Reformed soteriology, and biblical authority.

churches.assessment: The Way Baptist Church (formerly Skyline Baptist Church) is a Southern Baptist congregation in Branson, Missouri — confirmed in the SBC Churches Directory. The church is described as 'family-integrated' with 'expository preaching' and 'music lyrics focused on biblical truth' — three markers that signal a Word-centered, no-nonsense congregation. Multiple weekly services (three on Sunday plus Wednesday Bible Study) indicate a serious, committed fellowship. The family-integrated model means children worship alongside adults rather than being separated — a theologically intentional choice that reinforces household unity and parental discipleship. SBC affiliation provides BFM 2000 accountability on inerrancy, complementarianism, and soteriology. The main unknown is current pastoral leadership — Norm Howell is listed as a former pastor. Verify current leadership before visiting. Strong candidate for men seeking a doctrinally sound, family-centered SBC church in the Branson/southwest Missouri area.
churches.gender_detail: SBC requires male-only pastors per Baptist Faith & Message 2000; family-integrated model reinforces patriarchal household structure
churches.denomination_detail: Southern Baptist Convention — confirmed via churches.sbc.net

churches.name: Veritas Bible Church

score_notes.christology: Scripture-centered; affirms Jesus as the Word of eternal life (John 6:68-69).
score_notes.scripture: Strong emphasis on studying Scripture together; Bible is central to identity. References John 8:31-32, Psalm 19:7-9.
score_notes.gender: PATRIARCHAL — per member testimony (Vlad Yakubets): "Men are the rulers of God's world in every sphere of life." This is not halfway-house complementarianism — this is full patriarchal household vision. Green.
score_notes.leadership: Pastoral team with preaching pastor and lead pastor. Verify elder structure.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed/evangelical orientation evident from liturgical approach.
score_notes.cultural: Bible church tradition — typically resistant to cultural drift.
score_notes.denominational: Independent Bible church — no external denominational accountability. The independence is a structural risk, but the patriarchal culture and strong biblical teaching provide internal guardrails. Yellow.
score_notes.preaching: Expository approach evident from emphasis on 'examining biblical texts communally.' Active sermon playlists and YouTube channel.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Annual men's retreat. Men's small groups where men do things independently. No official "men's discipleship program" — but as Vlad notes, when a church is already structured patriarchally, a formal program is redundant. The church's entire culture IS men's discipleship. Green.
score_notes.mission: Active community engagement; Bible reading plans and resources offered.

churches.assessment: Veritas Bible Church in Federal Way, WA is one of the strongest finds in the Pacific Northwest. Member Vlad Yakubets confirms the church holds a PATRIARCHAL (not merely complementarian) view — "men are the rulers of God's world in every sphere of life." This is the full biblical manhood vision. Annual men's retreat and men's small groups provide masculine discipleship without bureaucratic programming. Expository preaching, Scripture-centered identity ("Veritas" = truth), Reformed/evangelical theology. The only yellow is independence (no denominational accountability) — but when the culture is this sound, that's a minor concern. Personally recommended by Vlad Yakubets. One of the few GREEN churches in the entire Pacific Northwest.
churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal — men as rulers in every sphere of life per member testimony. Not merely complementarian. Male pastoral leadership confirmed.

churches.name: Reformation Bible Church FL
churches.address: 3845 W Eau Gallie Blvd #103, Melbourne, FL 32934
churches.pastor: Titus (Father-led church) / Brandon Gish / Ben Bowman
churches.pastor_credentials: Reformed pastoral leadership; Right Response Ministries Christendom cohort connection
churches.services: Sunday (Lord's Day) 10:30 AM — family integrated service with potluck fellowship following

score_notes.christology: Reformed confession — Christ as sole mediator and Savior.
score_notes.scripture: Scripture as the only rule to direct how we glorify God. Sola Scriptura.
score_notes.gender: Father-led church — explicitly patriarchal household vision. Strong.
score_notes.leadership: Father-led model under pastoral guidance. Family integrated.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology — salvation by grace alone through faith alone.
score_notes.cultural: Motto: 'By the Gospel and for King Jesus — We Build. We Fight. We Conquer.' No cultural capitulation.
score_notes.denominational: Reformed Baptist tradition. Likely 1689 London Baptist Confession adherent.
score_notes.preaching: Sermon archive available. Reformed expository preaching. Active on SermonAudio.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Family integrated model — men are discipled as fathers/husbands within family context. No separate men's program but the whole church structure IS men's formation.
score_notes.mission: Committed to justice for the weakest according to the Law of God. Great Commission focus.

churches.assessment: Reformation Bible Church in Melbourne, FL is a Reformed Baptist, father-led, family-integrated congregation committed to the sufficiency of Scripture and the glory of God. Their motto — 'By the Gospel and for King Jesus… We Build. We Fight. We Conquer' — signals a militant, Christendom-oriented posture that aligns with the Right Response Ministries vision. The father-led structure is explicitly patriarchal (GREEN on gender — not merely complementarian). Family integrated services with potluck fellowship suggest a tight-knit covenant community. Friend Michael Pflugrad is connected through the Right Response Ministries Christendom cohort of 2025. This is the kind of church the MOOP directory was built to highlight.

engagement.recommended_by: Michael Pflugrad (Right Response Ministries Christendom cohort 2025)

churches.name: Eastside Baptist Church
churches.address: 204 Eastland Drive North, Twin Falls, ID 83301
churches.pastor: Elders: Paul Thompson, John Martinez | Deacons: Dan Steineke, Scott Pierce
churches.pastor_credentials: Plurality of elders; 1689 confessional Reformed Baptist governance
churches.services: Sunday School 9:15 AM & 12:30 PM | Sunday Morning Worship 10:30 AM | Sunday Evening 5:30 PM | Wednesday 6:30 PM (Psalm reading, prayer, singing)

score_notes.christology: 1689 Confession Chapter 8 — Christ as sole Mediator. Orthodox Christology affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: 1689 Confession Chapter 1 — Scripture as sole authority. Inerrancy and sufficiency affirmed.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Men's Book Study active. Age-integrated worship means men are discipled as heads of households. Strong.
score_notes.soteriology: 1689 Reformed soteriology — unconditional election, particular redemption, effectual calling. Doctrines of grace.
score_notes.gender: Age-integrated worship, elder-led by men only. Adopted resolution on women's conscription — explicitly patriarchal position. GREEN — not merely complementarian.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of elders (Paul Thompson, John Martinez) with deacons (Dan Steineke, Scott Pierce). Biblical elder governance under 1689 Confession.
score_notes.preaching: Scripture reading and exposition central to worship. Sermons on SermonAudio. Expository.
score_notes.mission: Committed to 'advancing the gospel by evangelism, church planting, and shared missionary efforts.' Great Commission focused.
score_notes.cultural: Adopted resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription — engaged with cultural issues from a biblical framework. No compromise.
score_notes.denominational: 1689 Second London Baptist Confession with three noted qualifications. Confessional accountability. Strong.

churches.assessment: Eastside Baptist Church in Twin Falls, Idaho is a 1689 Confessional Reformed Baptist church with a plurality of elders, age-integrated worship, and a robust confessional foundation. Founded in 1972, this church holds to the full 1689 London Baptist Confession including the appendix on baptism. The elder-led structure (Thompson, Martinez) with deacons reflects biblical governance. Their adoption of resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription demonstrates a church willing to take stands on cultural issues from Scripture — not hiding behind neutrality. Men's Book Study and age-integrated model mean men are formed as household leaders, not shuffled into a separate program. Four services per week (Sunday AM, Sunday PM, Sunday School, Wednesday evening) indicates a serious, committed congregation. This is an all-GREEN church — rare and worthy of attention for any Reformed Baptist in the Pacific Northwest.

churches.name: Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York
churches.pastor_credentials: BA Elizabethtown College, MS South University, MA Liberty University, EdD Eastern University

score_notes.christology: Trinitarian orthodoxy. Affirms Apostles' Creed. Christ alone for salvation.
score_notes.scripture: Bible as final authority. Adheres to BFC 28 Articles of Faith. High view of Scripture.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Groups and discipleship available via Church Center. No confirmed dedicated men's ministry — verify in person.
score_notes.soteriology: Doctrines of grace (TULIP). Salvation by grace through faith alone. Reformed soteriology.
score_notes.gender: Complementarian. Male-only elders and pastors per BFC bylaws (2004). Note: female deacon on board (Helen Gemmill). Not fully patriarchal.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led with 3 elders (Senior Pastor + 2). Deacon board for material needs. Denominational accountability through BFC.
score_notes.preaching: Expository, sermon-based teaching through Scripture. Reformed tradition. Podcast sermons available.
score_notes.mission: Church planting emphasis. Elder Alex Kocman directs communications for ABWE (international missions). Bold witness central.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language. Conservative Reformed stance. Family-focused mission statement.
score_notes.denominational: Bible Fellowship Church denomination. Accountable to BFC conference. Self-governing under elder board.

churches.assessment: Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York is a Reformed, evangelical, baptistic church in the BFC denomination. Pastor Wesley Bunting leads a solid elder-governed congregation committed to the doctrines of grace and expository preaching. The church's mission — 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household' — reflects a family-centered, Great Commission focus. Elder Alex Kocman's role with ABWE gives the church strong international missions DNA. Two caution notes: men's discipleship is not confirmed as a dedicated program (verify in person), and the church holds a complementarian rather than patriarchal position on gender, with a female deacon serving on the board. Doctrinally very strong. Worth visiting.

churches.name: Forest Baptist Church
churches.pastor_credentials: Eastern Michigan University (undergrad); Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (graduate). ERLC affiliated.
churches.founded: Historic — originally founded by enslaved congregants who met in the forest
churches.services: Sundays at 11:00 AM (in-person, Facebook Live, YouTube, Zoom); Weekly S.O.A.P. Bible Study Tue-Fri 11:00 AM

score_notes.christology: Baptist — Trinitarian orthodoxy. SBC-affiliated through Kentucky Baptist Convention.
score_notes.scripture: SBC affiliation through KBC means Baptist Faith & Message 2000 — Scripture is inerrant and authoritative. SBTS-trained pastor reinforces strong biblical authority.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry confirmed yet — but Xavier McFalls leads discipleship ministry and weekly SOAP Bible studies run Tue-Fri. Verify if there is a men-specific component. Adonis Jackson serves as deacon.
score_notes.soteriology: Baptist — salvation by grace through faith alone. SBTS training is solidly evangelical/Reformed.
score_notes.gender: All-male pastoral team (5 pastors, all male). No female pastors or elders confirmed. Yellow until explicit complementarian/patriarchal household teaching is confirmed from sermons.
score_notes.leadership: All-male pastoral team: Lead Pastor Nate Bishop Jr., Assistant Pastor Michael McGee (preaching/teaching, bi-vocational at UPS), Assistant Pastor Alex Tenenbaum (community engagement), Samuel Tunde Abednego (Children's Ministry, SOAP Bible Studies), Xavier McFalls (Assistant Pastor, discipleship). No female pastors on staff. Strong male leadership structure.
score_notes.preaching: Pastor McGee specifically titled "assistant pastor of preaching and teaching" — indicates preaching is valued. SBTS training suggests expository capability. Need to watch sermons on YouTube (youtube.com/@fbcnewburg) to assess depth.
score_notes.mission: Active community engagement in Newburg/Petersburg neighborhood. Online worship presence (Facebook, YouTube, Zoom). Verify Great Commission language and missions partnerships.
score_notes.cultural: Historically Black congregation serving the Newburg/Petersburg community. KBC/SBC affiliation is a positive sign of conservative Baptist alignment. Verify no DEI/CRT drift in programming.
score_notes.denominational: Kentucky Baptist Convention (SBC affiliate). Listed on kybaptist.org. Strong denominational accountability. Pastor trained at SBTS — the flagship SBC seminary in Louisville.

churches.assessment: Forest Baptist Church is a historic predominantly Black Baptist congregation in Louisville's Newburg neighborhood — tracing back to enslaved congregants who gathered in the forest. Now led by Pastor Nate Bishop Jr. (SBTS graduate), with a strong all-male pastoral team of 5: Bishop (Lead), McGee (preaching/teaching), Tenenbaum (community), Abednego (children/Bible study), McFalls (discipleship). KBC/SBC affiliated — strong denominational accountability. Weekly SOAP Bible studies Tue-Fri show serious devotional investment. Online presence via Facebook, YouTube, and Zoom. churches.assessment: The Trinity Church is Mark Driscoll's post-Mars Hill comeback church in Scottsdale, AZ. Theologically, Driscoll is one of the strongest Reformed voices in America — his Christology, soteriology, complementarian gender theology, and expository preaching are excellent. He has been one of the most influential voices for masculine Christianity. However, the Mars Hill collapse (2014) involved serious allegations of spiritual abuse, authoritarian leadership, and plagiarism. Driscoll was removed by his own elder board. The critical question is whether the pattern has changed. Visit with discernment and evaluate the accountability structure before committing your family.

churches.assessment: First Baptist San Antonio is a historic downtown SBC church (est. ~1861) led by Senior Pastor Chris Johnson. Doctrinally strong: affirms Jesus as co-equal with the Father, Scripture as God's Word and 'supreme and final source of truth,' and salvation as God's free gift through personal faith in Christ. Notable strength: dedicated men's ministry ('Fearlessly Following Jesus') and a unique Bible study integration model where the same passage is studied across all ministries. The church broadcasts on KSAT-12 television, suggesting substantive preaching. One concern: women hold 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan, Tera Kouba), which goes beyond traditional complementarian support roles while stopping short of 'Pastor' titles. The senior pastoral role remains male. Extensive ministry portfolio including Spanish and Asian/international outreach. churches.assessment: Park Cities Baptist Church is a large Dallas megachurch (10,000 members, est. 1939) led by Dr. Jeff Warren since 2010. The church withdrew from the SBC in October 2024 specifically over the convention's push to restrict female pastors — a significant red flag for complementarian evaluation. Pastor Warren has publicly advocated for women in ministry, stating Jesus 'did not genderize the Great Commission.' The church affirms the 1963 Baptist Faith & Message (notably NOT the stricter 2000 version) and states men and women 'serve equally alongside each other.' Women serve on the Board of Trustees and chair standing committees. While the church maintains orthodox Christology, gospel-centered language, and active mission engagement, the explicit egalitarian trajectory places it in the RED category for gender/biblical design. The church remains affiliated with Texas Baptists (BGCT) and Dallas Baptist Association but has reduced denominational accountability after leaving the SBC. Not recommended for men seeking a church with complementarian convictions, but doctrinally sound on core gospel issues.

churches.assessment: Parkside Church under Alistair Begg is one of the premier expository Bible-teaching churches in America. Begg has preached verse-by-verse through Scripture for over 40 years with unwavering commitment to inerrancy, male headship, and the exclusivity of Christ. Truth For Life radio ministry extends his influence globally. The church is elder-led, missions-minded, and doctrinally rock-solid. A top-tier GREEN church. Note: Begg drew controversy in late 2023 for advising a grandmother to attend a grandchild's transgender wedding — he later clarified his pastoral intent but the incident raised some concerns among discernment circles.

churches.assessment: Mars Hill Bible Church was founded by Rob Bell, who became perhaps the most prominent example of evangelical deconstruction in the early 2010s. Bell eventually left the church, left evangelicalism, and now operates in a progressive/new-age spiritual space. The church he left behind carries his DNA. RED — Rob Bell's legacy is one of apostasy. Current leadership has not clearly repudiated his theological direction. Avoid.

score_notes.leadership: RED — The decision to ordain women pastors was a leadership decision that broke with historic Baptist polity and biblical complementarianism.

churches.assessment: Saddleback Church is one of the most influential churches in American history through Rick Warren's 'Purpose Driven' model. However, the church made the fateful decision to ordain women as pastors, leading to their disfellowship from the Southern Baptist Convention in 2023. This is not a minor issue — it represents a direct rejection of complementarian biblical interpretation. Warren's 'Purpose Driven' model also substitutes topical/practical preaching for expository teaching. Under Andy Wood, the church has continued on this egalitarian trajectory. RED — the ordination of women pastors is a deal-breaker on MOOP's rubric.

churches.assessment: Hillsong Church is a global charismatic mega-church network originating from Australia. The US campuses have been plagued by scandal — Carl Lentz (NYC) was fired for moral failure, and founder Brian Houston resigned after misconduct allegations. Theologically, Hillsong emphasizes experience over exposition, operates in a celebrity-pastor culture, and has weak accountability structures. Gender roles are egalitarian-leaning. The music is culturally influential but the theological depth is shallow. Approach with serious caution.

churches.name: Mosaic Church
churches.assessment: Mosaic is a creative, arts-heavy church led by Erwin McManus. McManus is a gifted communicator but leans heavily into cultural relevance and self-help-adjacent messaging. Theology is generally orthodox but thin on doctrinal precision. Gender roles unclear — yellow by default. Popular with young creatives in LA.

churches.name: Reality LA
churches.assessment: Reality LA was planted by Tim Chaddick and is now led by Jeremy Treat, a TGC-connected pastor with a PhD from Wheaton. Solid Reformed-leaning theology, expository preaching, and Gospel Coalition alignment. Strong candidate for doctrinally serious Christians in LA.

churches.name: The Rock Church

churches.assessment: Traders Point is one of the largest churches in Indianapolis. Restoration Movement heritage (Christian Church tradition). Aaron Brockett leads. Generally conservative evangelical theology with seeker-accessible style. Multi-site.

churches.name: Granger Community Church
churches.assessment: Granger Community Church near South Bend, IN was one of the early megachurches in the Midwest. Known for creative arts-driven services. Seeker-sensitive model. Verify current theological direction and leadership.

churches.name: The Crossing
churches.assessment: The Crossing in St. Louis is led by Keith Simon and Patrick Miller (hosts of Truth Over Tribe podcast). Reformed-leaning, expository preaching, thoughtful cultural engagement. Strong candidate for theologically serious Christians in STL.

churches.name: Christ Community Church

churches.name: The Chapel

churches.name: The Bridge Church

churches.name: North Point Community Church
churches.assessment: North Point is one of the largest churches in America, led by Andy Stanley (son of Charles Stanley). Stanley is a gifted communicator but has drawn controversy for his approach to Scripture authority, homosexuality, and his "unhitch from the Old Testament" comments. Seeker model prioritizes accessibility over doctrinal precision. Yellow with significant caution.
